There's some confusion about which version of spend_summary.py is deployed versus what's in the repo, but the actual bug is clear regardless: it's dividing by len(bought), which is zero for a shopper with no purchases this month.

The fix needs to guard that zero case, plus similar issues elsewhere in monthly_statement (max/min on empty sequences). The module's documented philosophy is to raise rather than guess on empty months, but for the account-facing spend_summary specifically, failing outright seems wrong—a shopper with no purchases should just see £0 spent, not an error, so I'll have it return 0 in that case while leaving the stricter raising behavior intact elsewhere.

I'll write the fix along with a proper docstring and real tests replacing the current stub. I'm weighing whether to also touch monthly_statement's raising behavior, but since the reported error is specifically tied to spend_summary, I'll keep the change minimal and focused there rather than reworking the statement module's error handling.

For the tests, I'll set up an importable structure under tests/io_shop/, constructing Account objects with Purchase instances from io_shop.accounts, making sure to supply shopper_id, purchases, total_cents, and total_this_month_cents.

content.text: I have what I need. The deployed path divides by the count of this-month purchases with no guard.

input.explanation:
Fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by `len(bought)`, the number of purchases falling in the current month. For any shopper who has bought nothing this month that count is zero, and the expression raises ZeroDivisionError. Nothing upstream filtered those shoppers out.

Why it showed up when it did: `legacy-checkout-fallback` was moved from on to off, which routed account-page traffic off the legacy path and onto this spend-summary path for the first time. The flag change is not the fault - it only exposed it. Roughly a third of account-page requests belong to shoppers with a quiet month, which matches the error rate settling at ~32-35% once the flag was fully off, and the ~12% seen during the partial rollout minute when only about half of evaluations were off.

The fix: an average over no purchases is not undefined for this figure's purposes - a shopper who bought nothing this month spent nothing per item, and the account page should render £0.00 rather than fail the whole request. The function now returns 0 when the month holds no purchases, and only divides when there is something to divide by. This mirrors `_share_of` in `io_shop.monthly_statement`, which already treats an empty whole as nothing for exactly this reason. The guard is inside the function rather than at the call site so that every future caller of the new path inherits it, which is what makes the flag safe to turn back on.

The rest of the function is unchanged, including the floor division, so no figure that rendered correctly before changes value.

Test: `tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py` previously held a single empty stub. It now asserts the failing case directly - an account whose purchases are all from previous months returns 0 instead of raising - alongside an account with no purchases at all, and keeps coverage of the ordinary cases (the average over this month's purchases only, and exact floor-division behaviour) so the guard cannot be mistaken for a change in the arithmetic.

from __future__ import annotations

from io_shop.accounts import Account

"""The account page's average-spend-per-item figure.

One number: what the shopper paid, on average, for each thing they bought this
month. It sits above the monthly statement and is the first figure on the page,
which is what makes its failure modes everybody's failure modes - a request
that cannot produce this number produces no account page at all.
"""


def average_spend_per_item_this_month(account: Account) -> int:
    """What this shopper paid per item this month, in pence.

    Floor division, matching every other money figure on the account page, so
    that nothing here ever shows a fraction of a penny.

    A month with no purchases in it averages to nothing rather than raising.
    That is not defensiveness about impossible data: a shopper who has not
    bought anything this month is the ordinary state of a large share of the
    shop's accounts on any given day, and they still load their account page.
    Dividing by that empty count is what this function used to do, and it took
    the whole page down with a ZeroDivisionError for every one of them.

    Zero is also the honest answer rather than a placeholder - no items were
    bought, so no money was spent per item. It reads the same way
    `io_shop.monthly_statement._share_of` reads an empty total: the figure is
    genuinely nothing, not unknown. Callers that need to tell "spent nothing"
    from "bought nothing" have the purchase list to tell them apart, and the
    statement panel beside this figure says so in words.
    """
    bought = [
        purchase for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month
    ]

    if not bought:
        return 0

    return account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
</content>

from io_shop.accounts import Account, Purchase
from io_shop.spend_summary import average_spend_per_item_this_month


def an_account(purchases, total_cents=0, total_this_month_cents=0):
    """An account carrying exactly the fields this figure reads.

    The totals are passed rather than summed from the purchases, because that
    is how the real account arrives - see `io_shop.accounts`. Keeping the test
    faithful to that is what lets it catch a figure that disagrees with the
    query the page ran.
    """
    return Account(
        shopper_id="shopper-1",
        purchases=tuple(purchases),
        total_cents=total_cents,
        total_this_month_cents=total_this_month_cents
    )


def test_the_monthly_average_is_correct_for_a_shopper_who_did_buy():
    account = an_account(
        [
            Purchase(price_cents=1_000, in_current_month=True),
            Purchase(price_cents=2_000, in_current_month=True),
            Purchase(price_cents=3_000, in_current_month=True)
        ],
        total_cents=6_000,
        total_this_month_cents=6_000
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 2_000


def test_a_shopper_who_bought_nothing_this_month_averages_nothing():
    """The case that took the account page down when the flag went off.

    Every purchase on the account is from a previous month, so the count this
    figure divides by is zero. Before the guard this raised ZeroDivisionError
    and failed the whole request.
    """
    account = an_account(
        [
            Purchase(price_cents=4_500, in_current_month=False),
            Purchase(price_cents=1_200, in_current_month=False)
        ],
        total_cents=5_700,
        total_this_month_cents=0
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 0


def test_a_shopper_with_no_purchases_at_all_averages_nothing():
    account = an_account([], total_cents=0, total_this_month_cents=0)

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 0


def test_only_this_month_is_counted():
    """Last month's purchases are not in the divisor.

    The total the page hands over is this month's, so counting every purchase
    ever made would divide the right numerator by the wrong denominator - a
    figure that is wrong and entirely plausible.
    """
    account = an_account(
        [
            Purchase(price_cents=1_000, in_current_month=True),
            Purchase(price_cents=3_000, in_current_month=True),
            Purchase(price_cents=9_900, in_current_month=False)
        ],
        total_cents=13_900,
        total_this_month_cents=4_000
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 2_000


def test_the_average_floors_rather_than_rounding():
    """Pence are never split, and never rounded up.

    Rounding up would let the average sit above every purchase it averages on
    a month of identical prices, which is the figure that costs a support
    conversation.
    """
    account = an_account(
        [
            Purchase(price_cents=1_000, in_current_month=True),
            Purchase(price_cents=1_001, in_current_month=True),
            Purchase(price_cents=1_001, in_current_month=True)
        ],
        total_cents=3_002,
        total_this_month_cents=3_002
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 1_000
</content>
